newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rising in Europe on July trade data.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rising in Europe on July trade data.

text.p: Ringgit was on the rise in early Europe on fund buying after ending almost unchanged in Asia following Malaysia's announcement of a 624.5 million ringgit trade deficit for July, dealers said on Monday.
This compared with a revised surplus of 551.4 million ringgit in June and a gap of 1.34 billion in July last year.
They said the ringgit was trading higher in Europe on a difference in perception between European and Asian traders.
"Some were predicting a deficit of one billion ringgit. It is much lower than that," a London-based dealer said, adding European buyers considered the deficit lower-than-expected.
At 1100 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.4995/05 per dollar against 2.5010/20 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Friday and an intra-day low of 2.5030 on Monday.
Immediately after the trade figures were announced around 0700 GMT, the ringgit hit a high of 2.5010, but retreated to its intra-day low soon after.

"Last week too the Europeans were trying to pull up the ringgit after KL closed. But, there was greater selling pressure from Singapore becaue of the (trade) deficit rumour," said a dealer with a Kuala Lumpur-based bank.
